summary: The proposal addresses a well-motivated and practically relevant problem (integrating Artemis with GitLab CI) and demonstrates solid domain knowledge. However, it fundamentally fails to follow the required proposal structure: three mandatory sections (Introduction, Motivation, Objective with subsections) and the AI Transparency Statement are entirely absent. Additionally, the figures and bibliography fall below minimum requirements (1 figure instead of 2; 5 references instead of 6–8), and the single figure is a prohibited sequence diagram. The schedule includes thesis-writing tasks and lacks agile iteration structure. Significant restructuring is required before this proposal can be submitted.

findings.title: Missing Introduction Section
findings.description: The proposal does not contain a dedicated Introduction section, which is a required section. The document jumps directly from the Abstract to Section 1 (Problem Statement) without an introductory section that provides context, background, and an overview of the proposal's structure.

findings.title: Missing Motivation Section
findings.description: The proposal does not contain a dedicated Motivation section. The required Motivation section should be visionary, explaining why the problem is scientifically important to solve and focusing on the positive aspects of having the solution. Instead, the proposal includes a 'Related Work' section and 'Expected Findings' which do not fulfil this role.

findings.title: Missing Objective Section with Subsections
findings.description: The proposal lacks a proper Objectives section. The required structure is: a short introduction, a bullet list of 3–4 high-level objectives (each fitting in one line), followed by a dedicated subsection for each objective (at least two paragraphs each). The current 'System Requirements and Top Level Design' and 'Expected Findings' sections do not meet this requirement.

findings.title: Missing AI Transparency Statement
findings.description: The proposal does not contain an AI transparency statement. This is a required section that must be written in first person, naming specific AI tools used, their purposes, the sections they were applied to, and must include a confirmation that the author carefully checked all AI-generated text.

findings.title: Only One Figure Included (Minimum Two Required)
findings.description: The proposal contains only one figure (Figure 1 on page 4). The guidelines require at least two diagrams, mockups, or figures. A second figure (e.g., a class diagram showing the bridge pattern, a component diagram of the Artemis–GitLab CI architecture, or a deployment diagram) must be added.

findings.title: Bibliography Contains Only 5 References (Minimum 6–8 Required)
findings.description: The References section lists only 5 publications ([Booch95], [Gamma95], [Hilton16], [Krusche17], [Krusche18]). The guidelines require at least 6–8 peer-reviewed publications. At least 1–3 additional relevant peer-reviewed sources should be added (e.g., on the bridge pattern in CI/CD integration, GitLab CI architecture, or assessment management systems).

findings.title: Figure 1 Is a Sequence Diagram; No Suitable UML Diagram Present
findings.description: Figure 1 depicts lifelines (Instructor, Student) with numbered messages (1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3), making it a sequence diagram. The guidelines explicitly prohibit sequence diagrams and require at least one suitable UML diagram (class diagram, activity diagram, component diagram, etc.). Replace or supplement with an activity diagram of the exercise workflow or a component/class diagram showing the bridge pattern binding Artemis to GitLab CI.

findings.title: Schedule Contains Thesis-Writing and Documentation Tasks
findings.description: The schedule includes items such as 'October: Writing . . .', 'November: Thesis ready for review', 'Review finished', 'December: Thesis', and 'September: Documentation for installation and configuration'. Per the guidelines, the schedule should focus exclusively on development/research work and must not include thesis writing, documentation writing, or presentation preparation tasks.

findings.title: Schedule Not Organized in 2–4 Week Iterations
findings.description: The schedule is organized by calendar months and individual weeks rather than in agile iterations of 2–4 weeks each. It does not reference the high-level objectives and does not follow agile sprint structure. The work items should be reorganized into named iterations (e.g., Sprint 1: weeks 1–2, Sprint 2: weeks 3–4, etc.) each with measurable, vertically integrated deliverables.

findings.title: Excessive Use of Passive Voice
findings.description: The proposal relies heavily on passive voice and impersonal constructions throughout. Examples include: 'the build plans must be updated manually', 'the base build plan is copied', 'changes are not patched automatically', 'the build plan is fetched', 'the build plan is made available', 'the code gets updated', 'it is possible to migrate', 'it is useful to teach', 'it would be useful to change', 'it is possible to determine', 'it will be possible to tackle'. Rewrite in active voice with clear actors (e.g., 'the instructor updates the build plan', 'GitLab CI fetches the build plan').

locations.quote: Later changes to the base build plan are not patched automatically to all student build plans, but rather the build plans must be updated manually in the CI Server.
the build plan is fetched. It could be transposed with a CI server which is dynamically updating the student build plan.

Since the benefts of using CI are quite high and nearly half of the developers who do not use CI mention a lack of familiarity as the reason for not using a CI service, it is useful to teach the concepts of CI at university

findings.title: Inconsistent Terminology: 'CI Server' vs. 'CI Service'
findings.description: The proposal alternates between 'CI server' and 'CI service' to refer to the same concept (e.g., Abstract: 'CI service', Section 1: 'CI server', Section 2: 'CI service'). Pick one term and use it consistently throughout the document.

locations.quote: migrate the CI service from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt CI service
Artemis currently supports Bamboo and Jenkins as a CI server for executing the tests.
Furthermore, the CI service should be part of the VC server to reduce additional efort

findings.title: Forbidden Sentence Starters ('Since', 'As')
findings.description: Several sentences begin with forbidden words: 'Since' (Abstract, Related Work) and 'As' (Proposed Solution). Rewrite these sentences to avoid starting with the forbidden word.

locations.quote: Since some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to reduce the efort
As a result, instructors are able to update the build plan after the release of an exercise
Since the benefts of using CI are quite high and nearly half of the developers who do not use CI

findings.title: Abbreviation 'API' Used Without Prior Definition
findings.description: The abbreviation 'API' is used multiple times (e.g., 'via the API of Artemis', 'the Artemis API for configuration') but is never defined as 'Application Programming Interface (API)' on first use. Define it before first occurrence.

locations.quote: The build plan can be made available via the API of Artemis and GitLab CI is downloading the build plan for each execution of the test cases.

findings.title: Repetitive Filler Words ('Additionally', 'Furthermore', 'In addition')
findings.description: The words 'Additionally' (×2), 'Furthermore' (×1), and 'In addition' (×2) appear across the document as sentence-initial fillers. Reduce their frequency and restructure sentences to flow more naturally without these connective fillers.

locations.quote: Additionally, the base build plan is copied once after the student started the exercise
Furthermore, the CI service should be part of the VC server to reduce additional efort
In addition, universities will save time and money as they will need at least one less server.
In addition, either Ansible or a Kubernetes cluster can be used for automatic deployment

findings.description: The text says 'This process is illustrated in section 4' (Section 2) but never explicitly references 'Figure 1' by its number. Each figure must be referenced in the body text with its figure number (e.g., 'Figure 1 illustrates the top-level workflow…').
